newsitem.title: INDIA: Indians vote in Punjab state election.
newsitem.headline: Indians vote in Punjab state election.

text.p: Polls opened in India's northern state of Punjab on Friday amid tight security for the election of a new local government.
"Polling has started on a peaceful note," Brajendra Singh, chief polling officer of Punjab, told Reuters in the state capital of Chandigarh.

"I am suprised at the enthusiasm of the voters as I have received reports of long queues at almost all polling stations before the voting started at 7.30 a.m. (0200 GMT)," Singh added. Polling stations are scheduled to close at 4.30 p.m. (1100 GMT). Around 15.2 million voters were eligible to vote, officials said.
The election to the 117-seat state assembly will be the first local poll in two decades not overshadowed by Sikh separatist violence in which more than 20,000 people died.
State polls in 1992, which revived local democracy after more than a decade of separatist violence, were held in an environment of fear and overbearing security.
India has poured in 100,000 paramilitary soldiers to oversee elections. Police tightened security and sealed the borders of Punjab state with Pakistan.

"Patrolling has been intensified. We are checking vehicles on suspicion and also conducting raids at known hideouts of Sikh and Kashmiri militants," state police chief Sube Singh said in Chandigarh, the state capital.
India's troubled Jammu and Kashmir state borders Punjab to the north.

More than 20,000 people have died since a separatist revolt erupted in Kashmir in 1990. Dozens of separatist groups are fighting for either Kashmir's independence or for a complete merger with neighbouring Pakistan.
India accuses Pakistan of training and arming Kashmir's Moslem militants, a charge denied by Islamabad.
The counting of ballots in Punjab is expected to start on Sunday and results are likely to be announced on the same day, officials said.
